Initially created: 2025-12-17T20:38:41.707+09:00 by chris Translate the following text from Classical Chinese into English.
Requirements: 1. The text contains page numbers in square brackets, such as [01], [02], etc. - These must be passed through unchanged. - Each page number must appear in exactly the same position in the translation as in the source. - The number of page markers in the output must match the input exactly.
2. Personal names, place names, titles, and other proper nouns should be rendered in Hànyǔ Pīnyīn with tone marks.
3. Do NOT transcribe the full Classical Chinese text into Pinyin.
4. Do NOT include explanatory notes, annotations, or commentary — output only the English translation.
5. The target language is English.

p.seg: Basic Annals 1: Emperor Wǔ, Part 1
Gāozǔ Wǔ Huángdì, personal name Yǎn,
courtesy name Shúdá,
nickname Liàn'ér,
was a native of Zhōngdū Lǐ, Nánlánlíng,
and a descendant of Hán Xiàngguó Hé.
Hé begat Cuódìng Hóu Yán.
Yán begat Shìzhōng Biāo.
Biāo begat Gōngfǔ Yuàn Zhāng.
Zhāng begat Hào.
Hào begat Yǎng.
Yǎng begat Tàizǐ Tàifù Wàngzhī.
Wàngzhī begat Guānglù Dàfū Yù.
Yù begat Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng Shào.
Shào begat Guānglù Xūn Hóng.
Hóng begat Jìyīn Tàishǒu Chǎn.
Chǎn begat Wújun Tàishǒu Bīng.
Bīng begat Zhōngshān Xiàng Bāo.
Bāo begat Bóshì Zhōu.
Zhōu begat Shéqiū Zhǎng Jiǎo.
Jiǎo begat Zhōu Cóngshì Kuí.
Kuí begat Xiàolián Xiū.
Xiū begat Guǎnglíngjùn Chéng Bào.
Bào begat Tàizhōng Dàfū Yì.
Yì begat Huái'yīn Lìng Zhěng.
Zhěng begat Jìyīn Tàishǒu .
begat Zhōu Zhìzhōng Fùzǐ.
Fùzǐ begat Nántái Zhìshū Dàocì.
Dàocì begat the Imperial Father, personal name Shùnzhī,
who was a clan younger brother of Qí Gāodì.
He participated in assisting the establishment of the dynasty,
and was enfeoffed as Línxiāngxiàn Hóu.
He successively held the offices of Shìzhōng,
Wèiwèi,
Tàizǐ Zhānshì,
Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn,
Dānyáng Yǐn,
and was posthumously granted the title of Zhèn'běi Jiāngjūn.
Gāozǔ was born in the year Jiǎchén, the 8th year of Dàmíng of Sòng Xiàowǔ, at the Sānqiáo residence in Tóngxià Lǐ, Mòlíng Xiàn.
From birth, he displayed extraordinary signs:
his two hips had fused bones,
the top of his head was prominently raised,
and there was a character on his right hand that read
"Wǔ".
When the Emperor grew up,
he was extensively learned and widely informed,
fond of strategy,
and possessed both civil and military talents.
His contemporaries and peers all highly praised him.
The room where he lived was always filled with a cloud-like aura,
and anyone who passed by it
would immediately feel a sense of solemnity.
He started his career as Bālíng Wáng Nánzhōngláng Fǎcáo Xíng Cānjūn,
and was promoted to Wèijiāngjūn Wáng Jiǎn Dōnggé Jìjiǔ.
Wáng Jiǎn, upon their first meeting, was deeply impressed by his extraordinary qualities,
and said to Lújiāng Hé Xiàn:
"This Xiāo Láng will become Shìzhōng within thirty years;
beyond this, his nobility will be beyond words."
Jìnglíng Wáng Zǐliáng opened the Xī'dǐ and
invited literary talents.
Gāozǔ, along with Shěn Yuē, Xiè Tiǎo, Wáng Róng, Xiāo Chēn, Fàn Yún, Rèn Fǎng, Lù Chuí, and others, associated there,
and were known as the "Eight Friends".
Wáng Róng was brilliant and discerning beyond others,
and especially respected Gāozǔ.
He often said to his close associates:
"The one who will govern the world
will definitely be this person."
He was successively promoted to Suí Wáng Zhèn'xī Zīyì Cānjūn,
and soon after resigned due to the mourning period for his Imperial Father.
In the early period of Lóngchāng,
Míngdì assisted in governance
and appointed Gāozǔ as Níngshuò Jiāngjūn,
stationed in Shòuchūn.
After the mourning period ended,
he was appointed Tàizǐ Shùzǐ, Gěishì Huángmén Shìláng,
and was assigned to duty in the inner palace.
He participated in the meritorious service of strategizing with Xiāo Chén and others,
and was enfeoffed as Jiànyángxiàn Nán,
with a stipend of three hundred households.
In the second year of Jiànwǔ,
Wèi dispatched generals Liú Chǎng and Wáng Sù leading a multitude to invade Sīzhōu.
Gāozǔ was appointed Guànjūn Jiāngjūn, Jūnzhu,
and was assigned to Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ Wáng Guǎng for reinforcement.
When they were about a hundred *li* from Yìyáng,
the troops, seeing the might of the Wèi army,
hesitated and dared not advance.
Gāozǔ requested to be the vanguard,
and Wáng Guǎng immediately assigned elite soldiers from his command to Gāozǔ.
That very night, he advanced,
a few *li* from the Wèi army,
and went directly up Xiánshǒushān.
The Wèi army, unable to ascertain their numbers,
dared not press forward.
At dawn,
the city saw the reinforcements arrive,
and consequently dispatched troops to attack the Wèi palisade.
Gāozǔ led his command to engage from the outside.
The Wèi army was attacked from both sides,
so they abandoned their heavy siege and retreated.
After the campaign,
Gāozǔ was appointed Yòujūn Jìn'ān Wáng Sīmǎ, Huáilíng Tàishǒu.
He returned to become Tàizǐ Zhōngshùzǐ,
and held the post of Yǔlín Jiān.
After a short while,
he was sent out to garrison Shítou.
In the fourth year,
the Wèi Emperor personally led a large army to invade Yōngzhōu.
Míngdì ordered Gāozǔ to go to their aid.
In the tenth month,
he reached Xiāngyáng.
An imperial edict also dispatched Zuǒmín Shàngshū Cuī Huìjǐng to overall command all armies.
Gāozǔ and Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ Cáo Hǔ and others were all subject to his command.
In the third month of the following year,
Cuī Huìjǐng and Gāozǔ advanced to Dèngchéng.
The Wèi lord, leading over ten thousand cavalry, suddenly arrived.
Cuī Huìjǐng turned pale
and wished to retreat.
Gāozǔ resolutely stopped him,
but he did not comply
and hastily extricated himself.
The Wèi cavalry pursued them,
resulting in a great defeat.
Gāozǔ alone led his troops to resist the attack,
killing hundreds of people.
The Wèi cavalry gradually retreated,
and he was then able to form a defensive line to cover the rear,
reaching the boats by evening.
Cuī Huìjǐng's army suffered almost complete casualties,
only Gāozǔ returned with his entire force intact.
Soon after, Gāozǔ was made acting Yōngzhōufǔ Shì.
In the seventh month,
he was formally granted the titles of Chíjié, Dūdū Yōng Liáng Nánběi Qín Sìzhōu Yǐngzhōu Zhī Jìnglíng Sīzhōu Zhī Suíjùn Zhū Jūnsì, Fǔguó Jiāngjūn, and Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ.
In that same month,
Míngdì passed away,
and Dōnghūn ascended the throne.
Yángzhōu Cìshǐ Shǐ'ān Wáng Yáoguāng, Shàngshū Lìng Xú Xiàosì, Shàngshū Yòupúyè Jiāng Shí, Yòujiāngjūn Xiāo Tánzhī, Shìzhōng Jiāng Sì, and Wèiwèi Liú Xuān took turns on duty in the inner palace,
issuing edicts on different days.
Gāozǔ, upon hearing this,
said to his maternal uncle Zhāng Hóngcè:
"With governance coming from many gates,
the path to chaos has begun.
The *Shī* says:
'With three dukes in one state,
whom shall I follow?'
How much more so now with six!
Can this be allowed?
If rifts appear,
they will eventually exterminate each other.
To avoid disaster now,
this is the only place.
Diligently practice benevolence and righteousness,
and one can sit and become a Xībó.
However, my younger brothers are in the capital,
and I fear they may suffer from worldly calamities;
I must plan this with Yìzhōu."
At that time, Gāozǔ's eldest brother, Yī, had returned from a posting in Yìzhōu,
and was still managing affairs in Yǐngzhōu.
Hóngcè was then sent to Yǐng,
where he presented his plan to Yī, saying:
"In the past, Jìn Huì, a mediocre ruler,
saw the various princes contend for power,
which led to nine internal rebellions
and three foreign invasions.
Now, six powerful officials are contending for power;
each wields the royal authority,
controls the ruler, dictates edicts,
and desires to monopolize power.
Grudges quickly escalate into animosity,
and naturally they will destroy each other.
Moreover, the heir apparent, while in the Eastern Palace, had no good reputation;
he was familiar with his attendants,
a cruel and malevolent person.
Once he takes control of all affairs,
and acts as he pleases,
how could he possibly sit idly, merely assenting to others' words,
and delegate governance to court officials?
Mutual suspicion will accumulate,
leading inevitably to great massacres.
Shǐ'ān wishes to emulate Zhào Lún;
his intentions are already manifest.
For a lame man to ascend to heaven—
truly there is no such principle.
Furthermore, his nature is very suspicious and narrow-minded;
he will only bring about chaos.
The only ones who could possibly hold power
are Jiāng and Liú.
Shí is timid and indecisive,
Xuān is weak and untalented;
the 'overturning of the tripod and spilling of the food' [i.e., impending failure]
can be awaited on tiptoe.
Xiāo Tǎnzhī is suspicious and jealous,
constantly speaking to harm others.
Xú Xiàosì's talent is not that of a pillar of state;
he lets others lead him by the nose.
If a rift opens and conflict arises,
the state will surely crumble from within and without.
Now that we have the fortune to guard an outer province,
let us plan for our own safety.
A wise man seizes opportunity;
he does not wait a full day.
Before suspicion and defensiveness arise,
it is advisable to summon your brothers to gather in due time.
Afterwards, if mutual suspicion
arises, there will be no way to extricate oneself.
Yǐngzhōu controls the key areas of Jīng and Xiāng,
and flows westward into Hàn and Miǎn;
the soldiers and horses of Yōngzhōu,
numbering tens of thousands in an instant,
stand here like tigers,
observing the empire.
If the world is well-governed, we will devote our loyalty to the imperial court;
if the times are chaotic, we will eliminate the tyrants for the state.
Thus, we can advance or retreat with the times.
This is indeed a foolproof strategy.
If you do not plan early,
regret will be too late."
Yī's countenance changed upon hearing this,
and he did not agree in his heart.
When Hóngcè returned,
Gāozǔ then requested to welcome his brothers Wěi and Dàn,
who arrived in Xiāngyáng that year.
Thereupon, he secretly manufactured weapons
and felled many bamboos and trees,
sinking them in Tánxī,
secretly preparing for naval equipment.
At that time, his residence often exhibited five-colored swirling light,
resembling a coiling dragon,
with purple qi rising above it,
shaped like a parasol.
All who saw it found it extraordinary.
In the winter of the second year of Yǒngyuán,

news arrived of Yī's assassination. Gāozǔ secretly summoned his chief clerk Wáng Mào, middle-ranking officer Lǚ Sēngzhēn, assistant prefect Liǔ Qìngyuǎn, and records officer Jí Shìzhān, among others, to strategize.
Once decided,
on the *yǐsì* day of the eleventh month, he summoned his subordinates to gather in the main hall,
and said:
"In the past, King Wǔ convened at Mèngjīn,
and all said, 'Zhòu can be attacked.'
Now, the depraved ruler's wickedness is complete,
his tyranny and cruelty extreme;
he has executed court officials,
leaving few survivors.
The people are in misery,
and Heaven commands his destruction.
You all share the same hatred for evil;
let us together initiate this righteous undertaking.
Titles of dukes, marquises, generals, and ministers
truly lie in this day.
Each of you, exert your merits to the utmost,
and I will not break my word."
On that day, the battle standard was erected.
Thereupon, he gathered over ten thousand armored soldiers,
over a thousand horses,
and three thousand boats,
using the bamboo and wood from Tánxī to equip the ships.
Initially,
Dōnghūn had appointed Liú Shānyáng as the Grand Administrator of Bāxī,
providing him with three thousand elite troops,
and sent him to pass through Jīngzhōu to carry out the mission of assisting Xiāo Yǐngzhòu in attacking Xiāngyáng.
Gāozǔ knew of their plan,
and so dispatched staff officers Wáng Tiānhǔ and Páng Qìngguó to Jiānglíng,
where they delivered letters to all the provincial offices.
When Shānyáng ascended westward,
Gāozǔ said to his generals:
"Jīngzhōu originally feared the people of Xiāngyáng.
Furthermore, with the saying 'when the lips are gone, the teeth feel cold,'
they are naturally in a critical situation,
so how can they not secretly agree with us?
If I were to command the armies of Jīng and Yōng,
and sweep clean the eastern region,
even if Hán Xìn and Bái Qǐ were reborn,
they would be unable to formulate a strategy.
How much more so with such an incompetent and deluded ruler,
who only commands a mob of compliant executioners?
I can make Shānyáng surrender as soon as he reaches Jīngzhōu.
All of you, let's see how it turns out."
When Shānyáng reached Bālíng,
Gāozǔ again ordered Tiānhǔ to carry a letter to Yǐngzhòu and his brothers.
After he left,
Gāozǔ said to Zhāng Hóngcè:
"The way of using troops,
attacking the heart is superior,
attacking the city is secondary;
mental warfare is superior,
armed warfare is secondary.
This is the case today.
Recently, I sent Tiānhǔ to the provincial offices,
and everyone received a letter.
Now, this dispatch is extremely urgent,
and there are only two sealed letters for the acting officials and their brothers,
saying, 'Tiānhǔ will explain verbally';
but when Tiānhǔ is questioned, he has nothing to say verbally.
The acting officials cannot communicate with each other,
and it is impossible for them to speak carelessly.
Tiānhǔ is a trusted confidant of the acting officials.
When they hear this, they will surely believe that the acting officials and Tiānhǔ are concealing the matter together,
which will cause everyone to become suspicious.
Shānyáng, misled by the multitude of voices,
will certainly suspect disloyalty,
and they will inevitably leak our plans.
This is to stabilize a province by sending two empty envelopes."
Shānyáng reached Jiāng'ān,
and upon hearing this,
indeed became suspicious and did not advance.
Yǐngzhòu was greatly alarmed,
and so he beheaded Tiānhǔ,
and sent his head to Shānyáng.
Shānyáng believed him,
and with several tens of men, galloped in.
Yǐngzhòu, who had hidden armed men, beheaded him,
and sent his head to Gāozǔ.
He then reported on the proposal for the Nánkāng Wáng's title,
and further said:
"This month is not auspicious,
we must wait until February of next year;
to hastily advance troops now,
I fear, is not a strategy for the ancestral temple."
Gāozǔ replied:
"Now we have a hundred thousand armored soldiers,
and our provisions are depleting.
Moreover, we rely on righteous hearts,
a temporary surge of bravery,
and with things happening one after another,
we still fear doubt and slackening;
if we delay troops for ten tens of days,
remorse will surely arise.
If even children form factions,
then great affairs cannot be accomplished.
Now the planet Venus appears in the west,
and we act righteously.
With the opportune time and human planning,
what disadvantage can there be?
The arrangements are already made,
how can we stop in the middle?
In ancient times, King Wǔ attacked Zhòu,
going against the Grand Commander of the Year.
Did he still need to wait for the year and month?"
Cáo Jǐngzōng, Grand Administrator of Jìnglíng, sent Dù Sīchōng to persuade Gāozǔ to welcome the Nánkāng Wáng and make Xiāngyáng the capital,
to await the formal bestowal of the title,
and then advance the army.
Gāozǔ did not agree.
Wáng Mào also privately said to Zhāng Hóngcè:
"I serve Your Excellency,
and am bound by righteousness to advance or retreat with you;
however, by placing the Nánkāng Wáng in other people's hands now,
they will then hold the Son of Heaven to command the feudal lords,
and Your Excellency will go forward to be commanded by others.
How can this be a plan for weathering the cold?"
Hóngcè reported it,
and Gāozǔ said:
"If the great enterprise ahead does not succeed,
then naturally both orchids and mugwort will be burned together;
but if the achievements are established,
and our prestige awe-inspiring throughout the four seas,
commanding all under heaven,
who would dare not obey!
How can I be an ordinary person accepting others' commands?
When we reach Shíchéng,
I will personally clarify this to Wáng Mào and Cáo Jǐngzōng."
They established Xīnyě Commandery in Miànnán
to gather the newly surrendered.
In the second month of the third year,
the Nánkāng Wáng was appointed Grand Chancellor,
and Gāozǔ was made General Who Conquers the East,
granted a set of drums and pipes.
On the day Wùshēn,
Gāozǔ departed Xiāngyáng.
He left his younger brother Wěi to guard Xiāngyáng city,
overseeing all provincial affairs, and his younger brother Dàn to guard the camp city.
The Registrar of the Prefecture, Zhuāngqiū Hēi, guarded Fánchéng.
The Director of Merits, Jí Shìxún, concurrently served as Chief Clerk.
The Commander of Báimǎ Outpost, Huáng Sìzǔ, concurrently served as Registrar.
The Magistrate of Ruò, Dù Yǒng, concurrently served as Aide-de-Camp.
The Sub-Prefectural Clerk, Guō Yǎn, was in charge of transport.
A proclamation was issued to the capital: "Indeed, the Dao is not always smooth,
and times do not perpetuate eternal transformation.
Peril and peace succeed each other,
and darkness and light are not constant.
All things endure hardship before flourishing,
relying on many difficulties to reveal sagacity.
Thus,
when Chāngyì deviated from virtue,
Emperor Xiàoxuān rose;
when Hǎixī plunged governance into chaos,
Emperor Jiǎnwén ascended the throne.
Both opened new lines of succession and established foundations,
continuing the precious mandate.
This truth is verified by past classics,
and these events are clearly
recorded in past strategies.
The solitary tyrant has disturbed the natural order,
destroying the virtue of a ruler.
His treachery, depravity, and indulgence
have intensified with each passing year.
He inflicted cruelty in the year of his coming of age,
and planted danger in his childhood
days.
His suspicion and viciousness
manifested at every turn;
his tyranny, brutality, and foolishness
erupted with every incident.
Since the late emperor's illness progressed,
his joyful countenance was seen prematurely.
While the imperial coffin was in mourning,
he showed no
sorrow.
His merrymaking and banqueting
exceeded the ordinary,
and his strange and awe-inspiring attire
became excessively ostentatious.
As for selecting concubines,
there was no distinction between sisters.
When inviting attendants for his personal service,
aunts and nieces were indistinguishable.
The imperial harem gained a reputation for promiscuity,
and noblewomen were forced to wear soldiers' armor.
He even exposed his body,
wearing his underclothes inside out,
and would behead people in their midst
for
amusement.
He indulged in unbridled licentiousness,
driving people from the suburbs.
The old and weak drifted,
men and women suffered dire straits.
Bodies littered the roads,
and coffins filled the thoroughfares.
Mothers could not embrace their children,
and children had no time to mourn.
Robbery and plunder continued day and night,
one after another.
They hid by day and roamed by night,
without rest.
He indulged in debauchery and drunkenness,
singing and reveling in taverns.
He favored foolish
youths,
and was misled by evil enchantresses.
Méi Chóng'ér and Rú Fǎzhēn, mere servants and low-ranking individuals,
monopolized power,
executed loyal and virtuous officials,
and slaughtered ministers and grand administrators.
Liú Zhènjūn, a respected
maternal uncle,
was utterly loyal to the state.
Jiāng Púyè, a prominent maternal relative,
served the emperor with utmost sincerity.
Xiāo Lǐngjūn, a distant relative,
was committed to supporting the pillar of the state.
Xú Sīkōng,
On the *xīnyǒu* day of the second month,
the subordinate officials of the government again requested, saying:
“Recently, by imperial command, we presented a memorial,
boldly expressing our utmost sincerity.
We have received a return order,
but it has not yet been genuinely accepted.
The officials are eagerly awaiting,
and are deeply perplexed.
We have heard that accepting gold from the government,
which great men do with magnanimous purpose,
or gracefully withdrawing to the corner of the sea,
which commoners do as a minor virtue,
is why Zhōu Gōng was not suspicious when Lǚ Shícéng [Lǚ Shí] rode in his carriage,
and Tài Gōng was not hesitant to accept a jade *huáng* as a gift.
Moreover, a worldly sage follows the path,
and his former virtue remains with the people.
In times of chaos and wilderness,
he sighs deeply like Wēi Guǎn.
In addition, during the campaign of Zhūfāng,
he relied on the Jīng and Hé rivers.
When the army returned triumphantly,
he greatly contributed to the royal house.
Although there were those who repeatedly spun cocoons to save Sòng,
and endured multiple calluses to preserve Chǔ,
looking at the past from the present,
what do these amount to?
Yet, feeling as if stealing a bell,
his功 *gōng* is doubted and unrewarded.
Heaven and Earth,
cannot endure such cruelty.
This is why a swift jade horse ran,
signifying the departure of Wēi Zǐ;
and a golden plate emerged from the earth,
announcing the injustice of Lóng Fēng.
Míng Gōng leaned on his saddle and stopped weeping,
arousing the will of the three armies.
Dwelling alone, he wiped away tears,
inspiring the hearts of righteous warriors.
Thus, he was able to make Hǎiruò and Dēngzhī [Dēng Qí] appear,
exhausting their efforts to bestow blessings.
Shān Róng and Gū Zhú,
bound their horses and followed him like shadows.
He took responsibility for their faults and consoled the people,
bringing order to chaos with one effort.
This was not boasting of heavenly achievements,
but truly diligent effort.
Moreover, Míng Gōng was originally a scholar,
who found joy in the doctrines of the sages.
His elegant conduct and plain theories
calmed both the refined and the common.
He did not study Sūn and Wú,
yet he encountered this divine martial prowess.
He drove away all the doomed populace,
and saved the customs that were destined to be enfeoffed.
If the tortoise shell and jade are not destroyed,
whose achievement is it?
If he alone is a gentleman,
what place will Yī and Zhōu have? ”
Thereupon, he finally accepted the mandate of Xiàngguó Liáng Gōng.
On this day,
sixty-two types of extravagant and bizarre clothing of Dōnghūn were burned in the capital street.
Xiāngdōng Wáng Bǎozhì plotted rebellion
and was granted death.
An edict posthumously conferred upon Liáng Gōng’s former wife the title of Liáng Fēi.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Chén Wénxīng, the troop commander of Nánwǔzhōu, while digging a well within Huánchéng,
found two carved jade *qílín*, two carved golden jade *bì*, and two crystal rings.
Furthermore, Yáng Zhān, the magistrate of Jiànkāng, reported that phoenixes were seen under the paulownia trees in Lǐ, a village in his county.
Xuāndé Huánghòu praised the auspicious signs,
and they were presented to the Xiàngguófǔ.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
an edict stated:
“The state of Liáng has just been established,
and affairs need to be managed.
All important positions may be selected as before,
entirely in accordance with the system of the imperial court. ”
Gāozǔ submitted a memorial, saying: “Your subject has heard that if officials are selected by their words,
scholars will embellish their words;
if people are selected by their conduct,
people will exhaust their efforts in conduct.
It is said that talent is born into the world,
and success or failure depends on the times.
But the current
fashionable trends prevail,
and reckless competition has become customary.
Mediators boast and show off,
profiting from even the smallest gains.
This leads to the gates of officialdom
being crowded.
It is not merely that they brave the sun and rain,
not
avoiding heat or cold,
but they also gather their shoes and lean on their staffs,
sure to arrive in wind and rain.
This is truly because selection from villages and communities
does not follow ancient precedents.
They judge based on outward appearance and superficial qualities,
leaving them to manage trivial matters.
Furthermore, even those with great achievements like Shānhé and Liángbì,
lack the favor of imperial summons;
while Jīn, Zhāng, Xǔ, and Shǐ [referring to powerful families],
forget the decline of their old enterprises.
Alas,
how lamentable!
Moreover, genealogical records are erroneous,
and fraud is rampant.
People do not care
about the refinement or vulgarity of individuals.
Thus, those who falsely assume the lineage of good families
immediately become prominent clans;
those who carelessly tidy up their appearance
immediately become elegant scholars.
Those who have deep
faults against customs
are suddenly promoted and favored;
those whose grave trees have grown tall
are only then bestowed with honor.
Therefore, officials of previous dynasties,
all established selection rosters.
Those who were listed
had their own order of selection.
The rise and fall of family lineages,
and the good or bad of conduct and ability,
were either determined in advance,
or derived from public opinion.
Thus, guests could be easily distinguished,
and there was no need to sweep the gate for visitors.
[二四]In recent times, the system has declined
and fallen,
and the nine streams of thought have gone astray.
There are those who bravely retreat and forget advancement,
holding integrity and embracing truth.
However, the selection department sometimes considers them difficult to promote
because they have not yet made court appearances.
Or there are those who conceal their goodness
and hide their reputation,
burying themselves in humble dwellings.
They are also denied opportunities
because their names are not well-known.
One must present a name card and submit a petition,
and only then can one be an official.
This forces the modest
and encourages fierce competition.
Your subject humbly believes that from now on, the selection office should carefully review,
and establish rosters as before,
so that official positions match qualifications,
and names and realities do not diverge.
Then, people will know their limits,
and unsolicited requests will naturally cease.
Moreover, I have heard that an intermediate regulation stipulates
that prominent families may enter officialdom at twenty,
while lesser families must be probationary officials after passing the age of thirty.
To your subject’s humble understanding,
this is still not acceptable.
Why?
The establishment of offices and division of duties
should prioritize talent.
If the Eight Worthies, at a young age,
are suppressed even in humble positions;
while the Four Villains, at a young age,
are deemed worthy within prominent clans.
This would mean that families with hereditary
stipends
have no intention of doing good;
while commoners
freely indulge in evil.
How can this be to promote virtuous conduct
and inspire future generations?
This is a truly great evil,
which
should be abolished.
Otherwise,
it will cause the people of Zhōu to weep by the roadside,
and the officials of Jìn to sigh over fishing and hunting.
Furthermore, vulgarity and competition are prevalent,
and few people have a mind to withdraw.
If there is a limit
on age to enter court,
they will surely increase their age to seek office.
Thus, outwardly and truly ignorant children
will already claim to be over thirty in their registers.
This defiles the doctrines of the sages,
and is most egregious.
Your subject oversees both internal and external affairs,
and bears this responsibility with worry.
Regarding the successes and failures of court administration,
it is my duty not to conceal them.
I humbly beg Your Majesty to show your sagely and virtuous disposition,
and grant your
attention.
Then, proper human relations will naturally be harmonious,
and laws and regulations will be just. ”
An edict commanded that Gāozǔ’s memorial be put into effect.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
an edict said: “Sōng Gāo is a great mountain,
matching Heaven, thus its fame flows forth;
the grand opening of Nányáng,
thus its霸 *bà* virtue shines forth.
Loyalty and sincerity were observed by the Emperor;
the vassal lord received a high noble title,
revered.
Diligently serving the royal house,
Jī Gōng 姬公 extended the lands of the feudatories.
The former kings' excellent ordinances
were promulgated in all regions and records,
granting long-lasting prosperity to the populace;
none failed to follow these.
The Imperial Chancellor, Liáng Gōng 梁公,
embodies this supreme wisdom,
possessing a sagely and expansive depth.
His civilizing influence permeates internally,
his martial achievements flourish externally.
By promoting and establishing feudal lords,
his prestige and benevolence reach even distant
customs.
By training troops and teaching warfare,
his thunderous might reverberates across ten thousand li.
When the Way was lost and the times were dark,
slander and wickedness flourished greatly.
How could it merely be that the ancestral altars were in peril, and the divine regalia had no master?
Indeed!
As for the annihilation of the populace,
the extermination of the gentry,
the remaining survivors clinging to life,
facing death each morning,
all living beings trembling with fear,
with no place to turn their feet —
thus the mountains and rivers were over
turned,
and vegetation covered the ground.
Compared to the time when benevolence covered the flourishing reeds,
and trustworthiness reached even pigs and fish,
how immensely distant are these two eras!
The Duke commanded his forces to gather
and march,
pursuing the sun's shadow in a long campaign.
However, the capital was in dire straits,
Fán 樊 and Dèng 鄧 were far away,
water and land routes were in sight of each other.
From Gūshú 姑孰
to Xiàshǒu 夏首,
the strong troops of Yánchéng 嚴城
relied on the rivers for defense.
The Duke proceeded along the Hàn 漢 River and floated down the Jiāng 江,
moving like lightning and sweeping like wind.
Boats capsized in the water,
and strategic strongholds collapsed like clouds.
Relying on this righteous courage,
no strong
enemy formation stood before him.
He saved the endangered capital,
cleansed our imperial domain,
extinguished the spreading prairie fire,
and spared those facing execution from house to house.
The vast multitude,
whose fate was not in Heaven,
and the boundless six
directions
all received his beneficence.
He rectified customs and restored the fundamental,
so the people did not lose their livelihoods.
Benevolence and trustworthiness proceeded together,
ritual and music flourished in unison.
Yī Ī and Zhōu 周 are not enough to compare with him,
while Huán 桓 and Wén 文
would be greatly ashamed of their virtue.
However, his enfeoffment as a feudal lord,
with his territory extending only to Qín 秦 and Chǔ 楚,
is not sufficient to adequately reward his brilliant achievements
and truly acknowledge his great merit.
This is truly because the Duke's humility is fundamental,
manifesting itself in every action,
so his auspicious commendations have not yet been fully presented,
and we await them with increasing anticipation day by day.
It is appropriate to elevate this ritual rank
to truly fulfill the expectations of all, far and near.
Let Liáng Gōng 梁公 be advanced to the rank of King.

With the ten commanderies of Nánqiáo 南譙 and Lújiāng 廬江 from Yùzhōu 豫州, Xúnyáng 尋陽 from Jiāngzhōu 江州, Wǔchāng 武昌 and Xīyáng 西陽 from Yǐngzhōu 郢州, Nánlángyé 南琅邪, Nándōnghǎi 南東海, and Jìnlíng 晉陵 from Nánxúzhōu 南徐州, and Línhǎi 臨海 and Yǒngjiā 永嘉 from Yángzhōu
, these ten commanderies
are added to the State of Liáng 梁,
making twenty commanderies in total.
His positions as Imperial Chancellor, Grand Administrator of Yángzhōu 揚州, and General-in-Chief of Cavalry remain as before.
The Duke firmly declined.
An imperial edict ordered the cessation of further memorials.
The Imperial Chancellor's Chief Clerk of the Left, Wáng Yíng 王瑩, and others, led the hundred officials in earnestly imploring him.
On the *xīnmǎo* 辛卯 day of the third month,
Dài Chē 戴車, the warden of Huáyángluó 華陽邏 in Yánlíng Xiàn 延陵縣, submitted a dispatch stating:
"On the *yǐyǒu* 乙酉 day of the twelfth month,
sweet dew descended upon Máoshān 茅山,
spreading for several li.
On the *jǐyǒu* 己酉 day of the first month,
the warden Pān Dàogài 潘道蓋 found a hairy turtle in a rock cave on the mountain.
On the *xīnyǒu* 辛酉 day of the second month,
the warden Xú Língfú 徐靈符 again saw a white musk deer to the east of the mountain.
At dawn on the *bǐngyín* 丙寅 day,
clouds and mists gathered from all four directions on the mountain.
Soon there appeared a black and yellow color,
shaped like a dragon,
over ten *zhàng* 長 in length,
alternately hidden and revealed,
until after a long time it ascended to heaven from the northwest."
On the *dīngmǎo* 丁卯 day,
Mǎ Yuánhé 馬元和, the Cìshǐ 刺史 of Yǒngzhōu 兗州, reported:
"In the Dōngpíng Jùn 東平郡, Shòuzhāng Xiàn 壽張縣, under my jurisdiction, a *zōuyú* 騶虞 was seen."
On the *guǐsì* 癸巳 day,
he accepted the title of King of Liáng 梁.
The command stated:
"I, the lonely one, with my limited ability,
am entrusted with the national helm.
Although I diligently strive day and night,
my mind is set on promoting good governance,
yet cultivating virtue and bringing peace to the people
is still far off.
The sagely court, remembering old precedents,
has bestowed this great appointment upon me.
The grand ceremony of enfeoffing a duke,
is on par with the achievements of past exemplars;
the auspicious bounty is profoundly bestowed,
the rituals are clearly exalted.
To merely cling to my humble resolve
would ultimately impede understanding.
The multitude of dukes and all officials
have repeatedly urged and encouraged this,
compelling this thick-faced one
to accept this propitious fortune.
I gaze upon Kūn 昆 and Péng 彭 with longings,
and admire Huán 桓 and Wén 文 with sighs.
I wish to promote the path of governance,
but know not how to cross the ford.
As the state domain is newly established,
and the feudal realm is renewed,
I wish to extend auspicious blessings
to the subordinate states.
Within the state, all those below capital punishment,
prior to dawn on the fifteenth day of this month,
shall all be pardoned.
Widows, widowers, orphans, and the solitary who cannot support themselves
shall be granted five *hú* 斛 of grain.
Those under the jurisdiction of the governorates and prefectures
shall also receive the same remission."
On the *bǐngwǔ* 丙午 day,
he was granted a king's crown with twelve tassels,
was to erect the Son of Heaven's banners,
have outrider escorts when going out and clear the way when entering,
ride in a golden-wheeled chariot,
drawn by six horses,
equipped with five seasonal auxiliary chariots,
with *máotóu* 旄頭 and *yúnhǎn* 雲罕 standards,
perform an eight-row dance,
and set up *zhōngjù* 鍾虡 and *gōngxuàn* 宮縣 musical instruments.
The titles and appointments of the King's consort, princes, and princesses
shall all follow the old precedents.
On the *bǐngchén* 丙辰 day,
the Qí 齊 Emperor abdicated in favor of the King of Liáng 梁.
The edict stated: "Verily, the Five Virtues succeed each other,
and the Three Reigns rise in turn.
Governing affairs requires the worthy,
and promoting talent reveals the sagely.
Thus, the imperial legacy perpetually flourishes,
and the kingly Way shines anew.
Replacing darkness with light
has been the tradition for a long time.
The virtue of Qí 齊 declined and weakened,
with repeated dangers and destructions.
Lóngchāng 隆昌's brutality and tyranny
truly defied Heaven and Earth;
Yǒngyuán 永元's incompetence and violence
disordered both men
and spirits.
The Three Luminaries dimmed again,
and the Seven Ancestral Temples hung precariously.
The imperial enterprise was almost shifted,
and all conscious beings knew of annihilation.
The fortune of our Gāo 高 and Míng 明 ancestors
was faintly on the verge of collapse.
Constantly contemplating the difficulties,
I carry the weight of being in an ice-bound valley.
The Imperial Chancellor, King of Liáng 梁,
was born with sagely wisdom from Heaven,
and possesses divine and spiritual martial prowess.
His virtue reaches the obscure deities,
and his achievements are equal to the Creator.
He stopped the rampant flow of the ancestral altars and land,
and rescued the populace from
utter misery.
He supported the tottering edifice,
and saved those drowning in the rushing river.
The nine regions were re-stitched,
and the four pillars were re-tied.
Lost rituals were restored,
and collapsed music was revived."
In the eleventh month of winter, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an edict stated:
"The establishment of teachings adapts to the times;
purity and corruption necessitate different governance.
Punishments change with the eras,
varying in severity.
In the past, the customs of Shāng (商) had not yet shifted,
and the people had been scattered for a long time.
Trapped in nets and fallen into legal penalties,
they were sought out day and night.
If all were to be subjected to the proper law,
then those in red garments (convicts) would block the roads.
If all were granted broad pardons,
then it would be difficult to govern the state.
Therefore, those guilty were allowed to redeem themselves,
to preserve the lives of the common people (*yuán yuán*).
Now, those near and far know the prohibitions,
and the prisons are gradually emptying.
Proceeding thus,
it is hoped that punishments can be abolished.
The system of monetary redemption,
should now be removed.
The regulation for redeeming crimes can be abolished."
That year there were many epidemics.
In the first month of spring of the fourth year, on the *guǐmǎo* day, the first day of the month,
an edict stated:
"Currently, among the regular selections of the nine streams (official classes),
those under thirty years of age,
who have not mastered one classic,
shall not be granted their first official robes (*jiě hè*).
However, if there are talents comparable to Gān (甘) and Yán (顏),
they shall not be limited by age."
One Doctor of the Five Classics (*wǔ jīng bó shì*) was appointed for each classic.
Jiàn'ān Wáng Wěi (建安王偉), General Who Guards the North (*zhèn běi jiāng jūn*) and Governor of Yōngzhōu (雍州), was appointed Governor of Nánxúzhōu (南徐州).
Póyáng Wáng Huī (鄱陽王恢), Governor of Nánxúzhōu, was appointed Governor of Yǐngzhōu (郢州).
Liǔ Qìngyuǎn (柳慶遠), Central Army Commander (*zhōng lǐng jūn*), was appointed Governor of Yōngzhōu.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the performance art of phoenixes holding books was abolished.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an edict stated:
"When performing suburban sacrifices to offer to the Emperor (of Heaven),
the utmost reverence must be present.
One must offer sincerity and exert oneself to the utmost,
yet still fear deviation.
However, in past generations, court women were often allowed to watch this ceremony,
with vast curtained palaces set up,
and decorated carriages glittering on the roads.
This is not how one reverently worships the azure heavens
and demonstrates sincerity to the supreme spirits.
The presence of numerous attendant carriages
was criticized by previous generations;
this practice should be stopped from now on."
On the *xīnhài* day,
the imperial carriage personally performed sacrifices at the southern suburbs,
and a general amnesty was declared throughout the realm.
In the second month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
Wèi Wèi Qīng Yáng Gōngzé (衞尉卿楊公則) was dispatched to lead the palace guards to block Luòkǒu (洛口).
On the *rénchén* day,
Lǐ Kǎi (李凱), Governor of Jiāozhōu (交州), rebelled by seizing the prefecture.
His Chief Clerk (*zhǎng shǐ*), Lǐ Cè (李畟), suppressed him.
A partial amnesty was granted to Jiāozhōu.
On the *wùxū* day,
Cáo Jǐngzōng (曹景宗), formerly Governor of Yǐngzhōu, was appointed Central Protector General (*zhōng hù jūn*).
That month,
the Jiànxīng Yuàn (建興苑) was established in Jiànxīng Lǐ (建興里) of Mòlíng (秣陵).
In the fourth month of summer, on the *dīngsì* day,
Liáng Míbó (梁彌博), the acting King of Dàngchāng (宕昌), was appointed General Who Pacifies the West (*ān xī jiāng jūn*), Governor of Héliáng (河涼) two prefectures, and King of Dàngchāng.
That month,
from the *jiǎyín* day to the *rénxū* day,
sweet dew continuously fell in Huálínyuán (華林園).
In the fifth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
auspicious grain grew in Shuòyīn Lǐ (朔陰里) of Jiànkāng (建康) county,
with twelve ears on one stalk.
In the sixth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
a temple for Kǒngzǐ (孔子) was established.
On the *rénxū* day,
Jupiter was seen during the day.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
Zhāng Guī (張瓌), Right Grand Master of Glorious Happiness (*yòu guāng lù dà fū*), died.
In the eighth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
the star Canopus was seen.
In the tenth month of winter, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
a northern expedition was launched.

Línchuān Wáng Hóng (臨川王宏), General of the Central Army (*zhōng jūn jiāng jūn*) and Governor of Yángzhōu (揚州), was appointed Commander-in-Chief of all northern expeditionary forces (*dūdū běi tǎo zhū jūn shì*).
Liǔ Tàn (柳惔), Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs (*shàng shū yòu pú shè*), was his deputy.
That year,
due to the expenses of raising the army,
princes (*wáng gōng*) and officials below them each offered state taxes and grain from their fields,
to assist with military funds.
In the eleventh month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Zhāng Jì (張稷), Minister of Public Works (*dū guān shàng shū*), was appointed General of the Palace Guard (*lǐng jūn jiāng jūn*).
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the sky was clear,
and there were three flashes of lightning in the southwest,
heard like thunder.
In the twelfth month,
Xiè Fěi (謝朏), Grand Commandant (*sītú*) and Director of the Department of State Affairs (*shàng shū lìng*), left his post
due to mourning for his birth mother.
That year saw a great harvest,
with rice priced at thirty *hú* per *shí*.
In the first month of spring of the fifth year, on the *dīngmǎo* day, the first day of the month,
an edict stated:
"In the past, during the Zhōu (周) and Hàn (漢) dynasties,
talented individuals were sought from all regions of the country.
In recent times, with corruption and decline,
the obscure and hidden are rarely reached.
When people are isolated and places are remote,
their voices are unheard and their situations unseen.
The integrity of scholars has declined universally,
and thus there is no encouragement.
How could it be that mountains and rivers, though possessing spiritual power,
are inherently partial?
It is truly due to knowing or not knowing, employing or not employing [talent].
I, with my meager virtue,
rule these myriad people.
Yet the fully enlightened and widely illuminated [talents]
are confined within their homes.
My flying ears and long eyes [i.e., intelligence-gathering network]
do not reach the four directions.
I constantly feel shame in my heart,
never forgetting it day or night.
Therefore, in all commanderies and states, if there are old families within the region who hold no court positions,
officials should be selected to seek them out,
so that each commandery has at least one such person."
On the *yǐhài* day,
Xiè Fěi, formerly Grand Commandant, was appointed Supervisor of the Central Secretariat (*zhōng shū jiān*), Grand Commandant, and General of the Guards (*wèi jiāng jūn*).
Shěn Yuē (沈約), General Who Guards the Army (*zhèn jūn jiāng jūn*), was appointed Right Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.
Yùzhāng Wáng Zōng (豫章王綜) was appointed Governor of Nánxúzhōu.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Wáng Yíng (王瑩), Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Protector General (*hù jūn jiāng jūn*),
with his former post as Assistant Director remaining.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Imperial Prince Gāng (綱) was enfeoffed as King of Jìn'ān Commandery (*Jìn'ān Jùn Wáng*).
On the *dīnghài* day,
Venus was seen during the day.
In the second month, on the *gēngxū* day,
Zhāng Chōng (張充), Grand Minister of Ceremonies (*tài cháng*), was appointed Minister of Personnel (*lì bù shàng shū*).
On the first day of the third month, *bǐngyín*,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Yì (翼), a cousin of Wèi Xuānwǔ Dì (魏宣武帝), led his younger brothers to surrender.
Liú Sīxiào (劉思效), General Who Assists the State (*fǔ guó jiāng jūn*), defeated Yuán Xì (元繫), Wèi's Governor of Qīngzhōu (青州), at Jiāoshuǐ (膠水).
On the *dīnghài* day,
Chén Bózhī (陳伯之) led his troops from Shòuyáng (壽陽) to surrender.
In the fourth month of summer, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
two bronze swords were unearthed at Rénshān (仁山) in Gāochāng (高昌) of Lúlíng (廬陵).
One eight-eyed tortoise was found in Shǐfēng (始豐) county.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
an edict stated:
"I, from dawn, residing in my fasting chamber,
am solely concerned with punishments,
the 'three punishments' and 'five hearings' constantly occupying my thoughts whether waking or sleeping.
Therefore, I placed the 'lung-stone' (a petition box) in the capital streets,
and increased officials in the imperial prison.
I diligently and personally review,
considering even the smallest matters with sincerity.
Yet, my discerning caution has not been fully effective,
and prisons are still congested.
I reflect with shame,
as if I had fallen into a pit.
Therefore, to all places of imprisonment,
I shall dispatch judicial officials and close attendants,
to take turns recording prisoners.
If there are any cases of injustice or prolonged detention,
they shall be reported in a timely manner."
In the fifth month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Zhāng Huìshào (張惠紹), Left Guard Commander of the Crown Prince (*tài zǐ zuǒ wèi shuài*), captured Wèi's Sùyù (宿預) city.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the vanguard of Línchuān Wáng Hóng captured Liángchéng (梁城).
On the *xīnsì* day,
Wéi Ruì (韋叡), Governor of Yùzhōu (豫州), captured Héféi (合肥) city.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Péi Suì (裴邃), Grand Administrator of Lújiāng (廬江), captured Yángshíchéng (羊石城).
On the *gēngyín* day,
he also captured Huòqiū (霍丘) city.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Venus was seen during the day.
In the sixth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
Huán Hé (桓和), Governor of Qīng (青) and Jì (冀) prefectures, and his vanguard captured Qúshān (朐山) city.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
the state of Dèngzhì (鄧至) sent envoys to offer local products.
In the eighth month, on the *wùxū* day,
the star Canopus was seen.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the Crown Prince's palace was constructed.
In the eleventh month of winter, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
because the military campaign had dragged on,
a general amnesty was declared throughout the realm.
The Wèi (魏) invaders attacked Zhōnglí (鍾離).
Cáo Jǐngzōng, Right General of the Guards (*yòu wèi jiāng jūn*), was dispatched to lead troops to reinforce them.
In the twelfth month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
Xiè Fěi, Grand Commandant, died.
In the first month of spring in the fourteenth year, on the day *yǐsì* (the new moon),
the crown prince was capped.
A general amnesty was declared throughout the realm.
Those who succeeded their fathers were granted one rank of nobility.
Princes and dukes downward were bestowed gifts, each according to their station.
Homage and congratulatory rituals from near and far were suspended.
On *bǐngwǔ*,
Ān Zuǒ Jiāngjūn and Shàngshū Lìng Wáng Yíng was promoted to Zhōng Quán Jiāngjūn.
Zhèn Xī Jiāngjūn Shǐxīng Wáng Dàn was appointed Zhōng Fǔ Jiāngjūn.
On *xīnhài*,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifice at the southern suburb.
An imperial edict stated:
"I reverently attend to the bright sacrifices,
and solemnly serve the supreme spirits.
I enter the bamboo palace and ascend the Grand Altar,
donning the fur robe and ceremonial cap to present the dark jade disc.
As the offerings of firewood and distant gaze have ascended,
sincerity and reverence have been fully expressed.
I ponder how to respond to the celestial origin [Qiányuán],
and broadly propagate moral instruction.
Yet, there are deficiencies in the path of governance,
and many aspects of law and administration remain obscure.
I truly await the assembly of talents
to bring peace to the myriad accomplishments.
Therefore, this is to be proclaimed far and wide,
to broadly gather exceptional individuals.
If there are those who are truly outstanding in their communities,
exemplary in their localities,
living in reclusion in their hills and gardens,
not seeking fame or advancement,
concealing their abilities and awaiting their time,
and have not yet been selected;
or those who are贤良 (xiánliáng - virtuous and good), 方正 (fāngzhèng - upright),
孝悌 (xiàotì - filial and fraternal), or 力田 (lìtián - diligent in agriculture),
they should all be immediately reported
with their names submitted in full.
They shall be elevated to public service [Zhōuháng],
and tested in the administration of various districts and cities,
so that all officials may diligently perform their duties,
and the myriad people have no hidden grievances.
Furthermore, as the severity of punishments varies with the times and laws are adjusted accordingly,
previously, punishments such as tattooing and nose-cutting
were used to replace capital punishment.
Yet, if one wishes to repent and reform,
the path is blocked.
All these may be abolished."
On *bǐngyín*,
Rǔyīn Wáng Liú Yìn passed away.
In the second month, on *gēngyín*,
the Ruìruì State sent envoys to present local products.
On *wùxū*,
the Old Man Star (Canopus) was seen.
On *xīnchǒu*,
Zhōng Hùjūn Wéi Ruì was appointed Píng Běi Jiāngjūn and Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ.
The newly appointed Zhōng Fǔ Jiāngjūn Shǐxīng Wáng Dàn was appointed Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the fourth month of summer, on *dīngchǒu*,
Piàojí Jiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Tóng Sān Sī zhī Yí, and Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ Wáng Mào passed away.
In the fifth month, on *dīngsì*,
Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ Jìn'ān Wáng Gāng was appointed Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the eighth month of autumn, on *yǐwèi*,
the Old Man Star was seen.
In the ninth month, on *guǐhài*,
Chángshā Wáng Shēnyè was appointed Hùjūn Jiāngjūn.
The Lángyáxiū State sent envoys to present local products.
In the first month of spring in the fifteenth year, on *jǐsì*,
an imperial edict stated:
"Observing the times and establishing teachings is what the king's governance prioritizes.
To benefit all equally
is truly to uphold the fundamental,
and changing customs to achieve good governance
all stems from this.
Recently, orders for reform
have been issued as needed,
but the essence of relaxation and strictness
has not reached its proper balance.
The people's sufferings are still numerous,
and uprightness and fairness are still scarce.
This is why I gaze upon the dangling pearls [on my crown] with heavy heart,
and sigh when meeting with jade and silk.
Let this be proclaimed throughout the four directions:
if there are government policies inconvenient to the people,
the relevant authorities shall list them and report them.
If local officials are commendably clean,
or if they are corrupt and harmful,
they should be separately reported,
and promotions or demotions will be carried out.
Senior officials should encourage and supervise,
and personally inspect dikes and embankments,
ensuring none are left unrepaired,
to avoid hindering agricultural affairs.
Taxes at passes and markets
may sometimes be unfair;
local authorities should review them in due course
and generously reduce the old rates."
In the third month, on the day *wùchén* (the new moon),
there was a solar eclipse.
In the fourth month of summer, on *dīngwèi*,
Ān Yòu Jiāngjūn Yùzhāng Wáng Zōng was additionally appointed Hùjūn.
The Gāolì State sent envoys to present local products.
In the fifth month, on *guǐwèi*,
Sīkōng and Yángzhōu Cìshǐ Línchuān Wáng Hóng was appointed Zhōngshū Jiān,
with his titles of Piàojí Dà Jiāngjūn and Cìshǐ remaining as before.
In the sixth month, on *bǐngshēn*,
the renovation of the Lesser Temple was completed.
On *gēngzǐ*,
Shàngshū Lìng Wáng Yíng was appointed Zuǒ Guānglù Dàfū and Kāifǔ Yítóng Sān Sī.
Shàngshū Yòu Púshè Yuán Áng was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒ Púshè.
Lìbù Shàngshū Wáng Jiǎn was appointed Shàngshū Yòu Púshè.
In the eighth month of autumn,
the Old Man Star was seen.
The Ruìruì and Hénán sent envoys to present local products.
In the ninth month, on *xīnsì*,
Zuǒ Guānglù Dàfū and Kāifǔ Yítóng Sān Sī Wáng Yíng passed away.
On *rénchén*,
a general amnesty was declared throughout the realm.
In the tenth month of winter, on *wùwǔ*,
Dānyáng Yǐn Chángshā Wáng Shēnyè was appointed Xiāngzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the eleventh month, on *dīngmǎo*,
Jiān Hùjūn Yùzhāng Wáng Zōng was appointed Ān Qián Jiāngjūn.
Jiāozhōu Cìshǐ Lǐ Cè beheaded Ruǎn Zōngxiào, the rebel of Jiāozhōu,
and sent his head to the capital.
A partial amnesty was granted to Jiāozhōu.
On *rénwǔ*,
Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ Wéi Ruì was appointed Hùjūn Jiāngjūn.
In the first month of spring in the sixteenth year, on *xīnwèi*,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifice at the southern suburb.
An imperial edict stated:
"I sit on the throne contemplating governance,
but the path of administration remains unclear.
Toiling from dawn,
many years have passed.
Now, as Tàihào governs the vital energy,
and Gōumáng initiates the season,
ascending to the center and moving towards the yang,
reverent sacrifices have been fully expressed.
It is essential to receive Heaven's blessings,
and spread this harmonious benevolence.
For the extremely poor households,
this year's three taxes shall not be collected.
For those without land or occupation,
provisions shall be assessed and granted according to local circumstances.
If people give birth to children,
they shall be given generous exemptions according to regulations.
Orphans, the elderly, and widows who cannot support themselves
shall all receive additional relief.
Proclaim this throughout the four directions.
All prefectures, commanderies, and counties
shall promptly handle lawsuits,
ensuring no grievances are left unaddressed,
as if personally overseen."
In the second month, on *gēngxū*,
the Old Man Star was seen.
On *jiǎyín*,
Ān Qián Jiāngjūn Yùzhāng Wáng Zōng was appointed Nán Xúzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the third month, on *bǐngzǐ*,
the Hénán King sent envoys to present local products.
In the fourth month of summer, on *jiǎzǐ*,
the use of sacrificial animals in the ancestral temple was first abolished.
In the sixth month, on *wùshēn*,
Lúlíng Wáng Xù was appointed Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the seventh month, on *dīngchǒu*,
Yǐngzhōu Cìshǐ Ānchéng Wáng Xiù was appointed Zhèn Běi Jiāngjūn and Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the eighth month, on *xīnchǒu*,
the Old Man Star was seen.
The Fúnán and Bólì states each sent envoys to present local products.
In the tenth month of winter,
the offering of meat sacrifices in the ancestral temple was abolished,
and vegetables and fruits were used for the first time.
In the spring, the first month, on the *dìngsì* day, the first day of the seventeenth year of Tiānjiān,
an imperial edict stated:
"The origin of joy
is the constant nature of all sentient beings;
to enrich the people and stabilize their homes
is the universal rule for governing the world.
I pity these common people,
never forgetting their plight at dawn,
and have frequently implemented strategies for increasing population and prosperity,
and often extended grace and compassion.
However, the number of registered households has not grown,
and migration still occurs.
Lightly leaving one's hometown,
how could that be their original intention?
Their assets and livelihoods are likely deficient,
and they have no means to return on their own;
the desire to return to their nest
cannot be appeased.
Now, as the New Year begins,
all things are renewed.
I wish to enable the black-haired people
to each settle in their former places.
This will ensure that no county has fallow land,
and no city has idle people.
The sounds of chickens and dogs will be heard between homes,
and mulberry and ramie fields will crisscross paths.
All people in the empire
who have migrated to other territories,
before the first day of the first month of the seventeenth year of Tiānjiān,
may be granted half a year of grace
to all return to their original homes,
and be exempted from taxes for three years.
For those who have wandered too far,
the travel time will be appropriately extended.
If there are those who are unwilling to return,
they should be registered as commoners in their current locality
and pay taxes according to the old rates.
If, after their migration,
there are no longer residences available in their original hometown,
the village officials, the three elders (*sānlǎo*), and other relatives
shall immediately go to the county
to apply for official land and official residences within the village,
to allow them to be accommodated,
so that those who yearn for their roots have a place to return to.

Regarding all those who, due to their involvement in market tolls and other offices, were found to have committed embezzlement, theft, or fraudulent reductions, and were consequently subject to confiscation of property,
their fields, residences, carts, and oxen
are the means of people's livelihood,
and should not all be confiscated.
A generous portion should be allocated and retained for them,
to enable them to sustain themselves.
Wealthy merchants and households
are also prohibited from abruptly acquiring and merging properties.
For those who have fled or rebelled,
regardless of the severity of their crime,
all are permitted to surrender
and return to the ranks of commoners.
If there are any who were detained,
they shall return to their original service.
These regulations shall be compiled
and made known to all."
In the second month, on the *guǐsì* day,
Zhènbei Jiāngjūn and Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ Ānchéng Wáng Xiù passed away.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Lǐng Shítou Shù Shì Nánkāng Wáng Jì was appointed Nányǎnzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the third month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Old Man Star (*lǎorénxīng*) was sighted.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Jiàn'ān Wáng Wěi was re-enfeoffed as Nánpíng Wáng.
In the summer, the fifth month, on the *wùyín* day,
Piàojì Dàjiāngjūn and Yángzhōu Cìshǐ Línchuān Wáng Hóng was dismissed.
On the *jǐmǎo* day, the kingdom of Gānlìguó sent envoys to offer local products.
Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn Xiāo Jǐng was appointed Ānyòu Jiāngjūn,
Supervising Yángzhōu.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Línchuān Wáng Hóng was appointed Zhōngjūn Jiāngjūn and Zhōngshū Jiān.
In the sixth month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Yìzhōu Cìshǐ Póyáng Wáng Huī was appointed Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn.
Zhōngjūn Jiāngjūn and Zhōngshū Jiān Línchuān Wáng Hóng, with his existing title, concurrently acted as Sītú.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Guózǐ Jìjiǔ Cài Zǔn was appointed Lìbù Shàngshū.
In the autumn, the eighth month, on the *rénchén* day,
the Old Man Star was sighted.
An imperial edict stated that for military personnel, servants, and slaves,
males aged sixty and above,
and females aged fifty and above,
should be exempted and become commoners.
In the winter, the tenth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
Zhōngjūn Jiāngjūn and Acting Sītú Línchuān Wáng Hóng was appointed Zhōngshū Jiān and Sītú.
In the eleventh month, on the *xīnhài* day,
Nánpíng Wáng Wěi was appointed Zuǒ Guānglù Dàfū and Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī.
In the spring, the first month, on the *jiǎshēn* day of the eighteenth year of Tiānjiān,
Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn Póyáng Wáng Huī was appointed Zhēngxī Jiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, and Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ.
Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ Shǐxīng Wáng Dàn was appointed Zhōngfǔ Jiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, and Lǐngjūn.
Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè Yuán Áng was appointed Shàngshū Lìng.
Shàngshū Yòu Púyè Wáng Jiàn was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè.
Tàizǐ Zhānshì Xú Miǎn was appointed Shàngshū Yòu Púyè.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices at the Southern Suburb.
Those who practiced filial piety, fraternal duty, and diligently worked the fields were granted one noble rank.
In the second month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
the Old Man Star was sighted.
In the fourth month, on the *dìngsì* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Old Man Star was sighted.
The kingdoms of Yútián and Fúnán each sent envoys to offer local products.

In the spring, the first month, on the *yǐhài* day, the first day of the first year of Pǔtōng,
the era name was changed,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
Civil and military officials were granted ranks for their merits.
Those who practiced filial piety, fraternal duty, and diligently worked the fields were granted one noble rank.
For especially poor households,
regular taxes were not to be collected.
The lonely, widowed, orphaned, and solitary
were all to be provided with sustenance and care.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Sītú Línchuān Wáng Hóng was appointed Tàiwèi and Yángzhōu Cìshǐ.
Ānyòu Jiāngjūn and Supervising Yángzhōu Xiāo Jǐng was appointed Ānxī Jiāngjūn and Yǐngzhōu Cìshǐ.
Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè Wáng Jiàn resigned due to his mother's mourning.
Jīnzǐ Guānglù Dàfū Wáng Fèn was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the kingdoms of Fúnán and Gāolì each sent envoys to offer local products.
In the second month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
the Old Man Star was sighted.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Gāolì Wáng Shìzǐ Ān was appointed Níngdōng Jiāngjūn and King of Gāolì.
In the third month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
the kingdom of Huá sent envoys to offer local products.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the King of Hénán sent envoys to offer local products.
In the sixth month, on the *dìngwèi* day,
Hùjūn Jiāngjūn Wéi Ruì was appointed Chējì Jiāngjūn.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Jiāng, Huái, and Hai rivers all overflowed.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Xìnwēi Jiāngjūn Shàolíng Wáng Lún was appointed Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the eighth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
the Old Man Star was sighted.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the newly appointed Chējì Jiāngjūn Wéi Ruì passed away.
In the ninth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
a star was seen in the eastern sky in the morning,
its light brilliant as fire.
In the winter, the tenth month, on the *xīnhài* day,
Xuānhuì Jiāngjūn Chángshā Wáng Shēnyè was appointed Hùjūn Jiāngjūn.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Dānyáng Yǐn Jìn'ān Wáng Gāng was appointed Píngxī Jiāngjūn and Yìzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the spring, the first month, on the *jiǎxū* day of the second year of Pǔtōng,
Nánxúzhōu Cìshǐ Yùzhāng Wáng Zōng was appointed Zhènyòu Jiāngjūn.
The newly appointed Yìzhōu Cìshǐ Jìn'ān Wáng Gāng was reassigned as Xúzhōu Cìshǐ.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices at the Southern Suburb.
An imperial edict stated:
"The Spring deity commands the *qì*,
and with reverence and solemnity, sacrifices are offered.
With sincere devotion, the earthenware and gourds are presented,
and the blue jade is prepared with proper ritual.
I wish to follow the covering of heaven
and spread this nurturing care.
All commoners who are elderly and solitary, or orphaned and young, and cannot sustain themselves,
the responsible prefectures and counties shall all take them in and care for them,
providing them with clothing and food,
always ensuring they are adequately provided,
until the end of their lives.
Furthermore, an 'Orphans and Solitary Garden' shall be established in the capital,
so that orphaned youth have a home,
and those with white hair do not suffer want.
If their lives end,
they shall be given a generous burial.
For especially poor households,
rent and taxes shall not be collected."
On the *wùzǐ* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
In the second month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices at the Míngtáng.
In the third month, on the *gēngyín* day,
there was heavy snow,
three *chǐ* deep on level ground.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
the Northern and Southern Suburbs were rebuilt.
On the day Bǐngchén,
an edict stated:
“To reverently comply with Hào Tiān (Vast Heaven),
observing celestial phenomena without error,
personally wielding the plow,
and dedicating utmost reverence,
thereby harmonizing with the constellation Xīngniǎo (Star Bird) above,
and instructing the people in seasonal tasks below,
managing the spring plowing in order,
the principle does not lie in the south.
Former dynasties followed this tradition,
but it deviates from the rites and regulations.
It is permissible to seek a fertile plain
in the Zhèn direction (east),
and establish one thousand mù there,
to truly conform to the old regulations.”
In the fifth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Wǎnyǎn Diàn (Jade Hall) caught fire,
and the fire spread to three thousand rooms in the inner palace.
On the day Dīngsì,
an edict stated:
“Princes, dukes, ministers, and officials
are now submitting memorials to congratulate on auspicious omens.
Although this expresses the sincerity of all officials for the state,
I feel much shame in my heart.
If my beneficence truly flowed like rivers and springs,
and compassion reached all living things,
the climate were temperate like jade candles,
and governance achieved great peace,
then auspicious signs would descend,
and there would be no shame in my virtue.
However, the path of governance has many shortcomings,
and pure transformation has not yet solidified.
How can this harmonize with the celestial order above,
and receive profound blessings from afar?
This merely further reveals my inadequacy,
and adds to its faults.
From now on, the congratulations on auspicious omens should cease.”
In the sixth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Wén Sēngmíng, General of Inspiring Awe and Inspector of Yìzhōu, revolted with his prefecture and defected to Wèi.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
Péi Suì, acting Grand Architect, was granted a staff of authority,
and led all armies to launch a northern expedition.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Elder Star (Canopus) was sighted.
Huán Shūxīng, Wèi Inspector of Jīngzhōu, led his troops and surrendered.
In the eighth month, on the day Dīnghài,
in Shǐpíng Prefecture, Shígǔ Cūn (Stone Drum Village) spontaneously opened up into a well,
six chǐ and six cùn square,
and thirty-two zhàng deep.
In the winter, eleventh month,
the states of Bǎijì and Xīnluó each sent envoys to present local products.
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùchén,
Yú Lóng, King of Bǎijì and General Who Quells the East, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East.
In the third year, spring, first month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Yuán Áng, Director of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Supervisor of the Central Secretariat;
Wáng Jiǎn, Administrator of Wújùn, was appointed Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs;
Wáng Fèn, Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Right Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.
On the day Gēngxū,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Xiāo Xù, Prince of Lúlíng and General Who Manifests Awe, was appointed Inspector of Yōngzhōu.
In the third month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Xiāo Píng, Prince of Bālíng, passed away.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Liú Duān, Prince of Rǔyīn, passed away.
In the fifth month, on the first day Rénchén,
there was a solar eclipse,
which was total.
On the day Guǐsì,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire,
and announced to the four directions.
The grievances and hardships of the people
were to be reported immediately.
Princes, dukes, and all officials were to submit sealed memorials,
and regional governors and prefectures were to recommend worthy, upright, and outspoken individuals.
In the autumn, eighth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
the construction of the two suburbs and the Xíjiàn (Ceremonial Field) was completed,
and artisans were rewarded with varying gifts.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Elder Star was sighted.
The states of Pólì and Báití each sent envoys to present local products.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
Yuán Áng, Supervisor of the Central Secretariat, was promoted to General of the Central Guard.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
Xiāo Dàn, Prince of Shǐxīng, General of the Guard, Kàifǔ Yítóng Sānsī (Establishing a Mansion with the Same Privileges as the Three Dukes), and General of the Palace Guard, passed away.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Xiāo Yuānzǎo, Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, was appointed General of the Palace Guard.
In the fourth year, spring, first month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifice at the Southern Suburb,
and a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
All who were destitute and ill
were to be relieved and comforted,
and this was announced to the four directions.
At that time, judicial cases were also handled.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifice at the Míngtáng (Bright Hall).
In the second month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
the Elder Star was sighted.
On the day Yǐhài,
the emperor personally plowed the Xíjiàn.
An edict stated:
“The meaning of plowing the Xíjiàn is indeed great!
It is from this that sacrificial grains arise,
and ritual ceremonies are established.
Ancient sagely kings all practiced this.
Mindful of the eight policies,
I establish these thousand mù,
and princes, dukes, and all officials
are respectfully diligent in its rituals,
completing the nine plowings,
and the fragrant offerings never cease.
Moreover, the winds and clouds harmonize with the seasons,
and the weather is splendid and glorious.
Observing this auspicious occasion,
I desire to add encouragement.
This is to be announced far and wide,
to widely open up good fields,
so that public and private farmlands
fully utilize the land's bounty.
If those who wish to engage in agriculture lack grain seeds,
they shall also be granted loans and relief,
always ensuring ample provision.
Filial and fraternal individuals who diligently farm shall be granted one rank of nobility.
The officials overseeing the ceremonial plowing
shall be rewarded with wine on a set day.”
In the third month, on the day Rénmín,
